## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose

Modular open-source platform for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with specialized verticals for e-learning and beyond. Vektra is designed as infrastructure, not as a consumer application. It provides building blocks for developers and organizations that need to integrate RAG capabilities into their systems, with a specialized vertical for learning management and knowledge delivery.

### 1.2 Scope

**In scope (Phase 1)**:
- vektra-core: RAG engine, LLM abstraction, conversation management, safeguards
- vektra-ingest: Document processing pipeline - PDF, Word, PPT
- vektra-index: Vector store abstraction, embedding, semantic search
- vektra-admin: System administration interface - minimal Phase 1, full Phase 2

**Delivered in Phase 2 (v0.2.0)**:
- vektra-core: Advanced pipeline, persistent conversations, query rewriting, reranking, safeguard hooks
- vektra-ingest: OCR via Unstructured, dual chunking, document versioning, batch operations
- vektra-index: Hybrid search (dense+sparse), Qdrant vector store provider
- vektra-analytics: QueryTrace storage, metrics aggregation, reporting API
- vektra-learn: E-learning vertical backend (LMS-agnostic), chatbot widget
- vektra-admin: Full dashboard (HTMX + Jinja2), RLS enforcement, rate limiting

**Out of scope**:
- vektra-moodle: PHP plugin - separate repo (Phase 2, not started)
- vektra-sdk-py: Python SDK - separate repo (Phase 3)
- vektra-sdk-js: JavaScript SDK - separate repo (Phase 3)

### 1.3 Constraints

- On-premises deployment support required (university infrastructure)
- GDPR compliance: configurable retention, audit logs, student data on-premises
- Multi-provider LLM support from the start (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama)
- Vendor-neutral vector store (pluggable backend, pgvector as default)
- Pipeline orchestration via n8n (external to Vektra)
- Configuration over fork: customizations via config, not code forks

## 2. Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Primary user persona: Platform Operator
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Phase 1 primary user is the Platform Operator (DevOps engineer or platform team member) responsible for deploying, configuring, and maintaining Vektra infrastructure. This persona has Linux/Docker experience, can read API documentation, and expects infrastructure tools to be self-documenting with clear error messages.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] All Phase 1 documentation written for Platform Operator skill level
  - [ ] No GUI required for core workflows - API and CLI sufficient
  - [ ] Error messages include actionable remediation steps

### REQ-002: WF-INGEST-001: Document Ingestion workflow
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: User: Platform Operator. Goal: Ingest a PDF document into the vector store for RAG queries. Entry conditions: Vektra stack running (docker compose up successful), PDF file accessible to ingest service, target collection/namespace exists or will be auto-created. Happy path: (1) Operator calls ingest API with PDF file or URL, (2) System validates PDF, (3) System extracts text content, (4) System chunks text, (5) System generates embeddings, (6) System stores vectors in index with metadata, (7) System returns success with document ID and chunk count. Exit conditions: Document indexed and queryable, ingestion metadata logged for audit.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Single API call initiates ingestion
  - [ ] Synchronous response for small documents (<10MB)
  - [ ] Document queryable within 60 seconds of successful API response

### REQ-003: WF-QUERY-001: RAG Query workflow
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: User: Platform Operator (testing) or downstream application. Goal: Ask a question and receive an answer grounded in indexed documents. Entry conditions: Vektra stack running, at least one document indexed, LLM provider configured and accessible. Happy path: (1) Client calls query API with question text, (2) System generates query embedding, (3) System retrieves top-k relevant chunks from index, (4) System constructs prompt with retrieved context, (5) System calls LLM provider for generation, (6) System returns answer with source citations. Exit conditions: Answer returned to client, query logged for analytics (optional in Phase 1).
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Query-to-response latency under 10 seconds (p95 measured over 100 consecutive queries with warm cache) with local Ollama
  - [ ] Response includes source document references in structured format: `{document_id, chunk_id, relevance_score, text_snippet}`
  - [ ] Each citation includes document_id (UUID), chunk_id (integer), relevance_score (0.0-1.0), text_snippet (first 200 chars of chunk)
  - [ ] Empty index returns helpful error, not cryptic failure

### REQ-004: WF-ADMIN-001: System Health Check workflow
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: User: Platform Operator. Goal: Verify all Vektra components are running and connected. Entry conditions: Vektra stack deployment attempted. Happy path: (1) Operator calls health endpoint (GET /health), (2) System checks: database connectivity, vector store connectivity, LLM provider reachability, (3) System returns component-by-component status. Exit conditions: Clear pass/fail status for each component, actionable error messages for any failures.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Single endpoint returns all component health
  - [ ] Each component status includes: name, status (ok/degraded/down), latency
  - [ ] Degraded components include remediation hint

### REQ-005: WF-INT-001: End-to-End MVP Validation workflow
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: User: Platform Operator (first-time setup). Goal: Verify complete Vektra installation by ingesting a sample document and querying it. Entry conditions: Fresh clone of vektra-stack repository, Docker installed, sample PDF available (included in repo). Happy path: (1) git clone vektra-stack, (2) docker compose up -d, (3) Wait for health check to pass, (4) Call ingest API with sample PDF, (5) Call query API with sample question about the PDF, (6) Verify answer references the sample document. Exit conditions: Query returns relevant answer from ingested document, total time from step 1 to step 6: under 30 minutes.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Scripted end-to-end test exists and passes
  - [ ] No manual configuration required beyond docker-compose.yml
  - [ ] Sample PDF and test script included in repository

### REQ-006: Phase 1 admin capabilities (consolidated)
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Unified administration interface combining scope and API specification. API Surface: GET /health (aggregated health with per-component breakdown, two-tier per REQ-025), POST /api-keys (create new API key, returns full key exactly once), GET /api-keys (list API keys masked, showing last 4 chars), DELETE /api-keys/{id} (revoke API key). UI Surface: Health dashboard at /admin (read-only visualization of /health?detail=full response), dashboard requires valid API key with admin scope. Constraints: No user management, no analytics, no document management UI in Phase 1. Admin endpoints require valid API key with admin scope.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] GET /health returns status for: index, core, ingest, database
  - [ ] Per-component status includes latency measurement
  - [ ] API key creation returns full key exactly once
  - [ ] Revoked keys rejected within 60 seconds
  - [ ] Health dashboard accessible at /admin with valid API key
  - [ ] No other admin features in Phase 1

### REQ-007: Phase 1 interaction mode: API + shell scripts
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Phase 1 provides REST API as the primary interface. No dedicated CLI binary. Shell scripts (bash) and a Makefile wrap common operations for operator convenience. Scripts are first-class deliverables with same quality bar as code.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] REST API is the sole programmatic interface
  - [ ] Makefile exists with targets: make health, make ingest, make query, make demo
  - [ ] scripts/ directory contains tested shell scripts for common workflows
  - [ ] Shell scripts tested in CI on each commit
  - [ ] API documentation includes copy-paste ready curl examples

### REQ-009: API error responses include remediation guidance
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: All API error responses include a 'remediation' field with actionable guidance for the Platform Operator. This compensates for the absence of CLI help text and supports REQ-001 acceptance criterion.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Error response schema includes 'remediation' string field
  - [ ] Remediation text is operator-actionable (not generic)
  - [ ] Common errors have documented remediation patterns

### REQ-010: Error response envelope schema
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: All API error responses use a consistent JSON envelope: `{"error": {"category": "TRANSIENT|PERMANENT|CONFIGURATION|UPSTREAM", "code": "ERR-{COMPONENT}-{NUMBER}", "message": "Human-readable error description", "remediation": "Actionable steps for operator", "retry_after": 30, "request_id": "uuid", "details": {}}}`. This schema is a contract. Breaking changes require major version bump. Field semantics: 'message' describes what happened (diagnostic), 'remediation' describes what to do next (prescriptive). Never combine these purposes in a single field.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] All endpoints return this envelope on error
  - [ ] Schema documented in OpenAPI spec
  - [ ] Error codes follow ERR-{COMPONENT}-{NUMBER} pattern
  - [ ] Remediation field never empty or generic
  - [ ] Message field is human-readable and non-empty
  - [ ] Message field does not expose internal implementation details (no stack traces, class names)
  - [ ] Message describes what happened; remediation describes corrective action

### REQ-011: Phase 1 error code registry
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Normative error codes for Phase 1 (MUST be implemented): Ingest: ERR-INGEST-001 (Invalid PDF), ERR-INGEST-002 (PDF too large), ERR-INGEST-003 (Scanned PDF detected), ERR-INGEST-004 (Vector store write failed). Query: ERR-QUERY-001 (No documents indexed), ERR-QUERY-002 (LLM unavailable), ERR-QUERY-003 (Query too long), ERR-QUERY-004 (Vector store read failed). System: ERR-CONFIG-001 (Missing configuration), ERR-CONFIG-002 (Invalid provider config). Auth: ERR-AUTH-001 (Invalid token - includes missing, malformed, unrecognized, revoked per REQ-041), ERR-AUTH-002 (Expired token - Phase 2 per REQ-041), ERR-AUTH-003 (Insufficient scope per REQ-041). Additional error codes MAY be added following the ERR-{COMPONENT}-{NUMBER} pattern. Registry stored at docs/error-codes.md.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] All 13 normative error codes implemented with remediation text
  - [ ] Error registry maintained at docs/error-codes.md
  - [ ] Each error code includes: code, category, message template, remediation
  - [ ] New errors added to registry before implementation

### REQ-012: vektra-index Phase 1 API surface
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Minimum API for vektra-index in Phase 1: POST /documents/{id}/chunks (store document chunks with embeddings), POST /search (retrieve top-k chunks by similarity), DELETE /documents/{id} (remove document and all chunks), GET /health (component health check), GET /stats (return document count and chunk count for operator verification).
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] All endpoints documented in OpenAPI spec
  - [ ] POST /search returns results within 500ms for 10k chunks
  - [ ] DELETE removes all chunks atomically
  - [ ] GET /stats returns accurate counts without full scan

### REQ-013: vektra-core Phase 1 API surface
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Minimum API for vektra-core in Phase 1: POST /query (execute RAG query, return answer with citations), GET /providers (list configured LLM providers and status), GET /health (component health check). LLM provider configured via environment variables (VEKTRA_LLM_PROVIDER, VEKTRA_LLM_API_KEY). Ollama supported for local/offline use.
- **Note**: Provider defaults amended by REQ-047. No hardcoded default provider at platform level.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Query endpoint accepts question text, returns answer with source references
  - [ ] Provider configuration via environment variables, no config file required
  - [ ] GET /providers shows provider name, status (ok/unavailable), model name
  - [ ] Empty index returns ERR-QUERY-001 with remediation

### REQ-014: vektra-ingest Phase 1 API surface
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Minimum API for vektra-ingest in Phase 1: POST /ingest (accept PDF file, return document ID and status), GET /ingest/jobs/{id}/status (return ingestion status for async polling, per REQ-040 path convention), GET /health (component health check). Ingestion is synchronous for small documents (<10MB). Larger documents return 202 Accepted with polling endpoint. Chunking uses fixed-size strategy with configurable parameters via environment variables.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] POST /ingest accepts multipart/form-data with PDF
  - [ ] Synchronous response for <10MB PDFs within 30 seconds
  - [ ] Status endpoint returns: pending, processing, indexed, failed
  - [ ] Failed status includes error code from REQ-011 registry

### REQ-016: Phase 1 input constraints
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Explicit input constraints for Phase 1 APIs: file size: max 50MB (configurable via VEKTRA_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB), query text: max 4000 characters, supported PDF types: text-based PDFs (Phase 1), scanned PDFs via OCR with UnstructuredExtractor (Phase 2), encrypted PDFs: rejected with ERR-INGEST-001, chunk size: 1000 tokens (configurable via VEKTRA_CHUNK_SIZE), chunk overlap: 200 tokens (configurable via VEKTRA_CHUNK_OVERLAP). Scanned PDF detection: PDF classified as scanned if text extraction yields < 100 characters per page (average of first 5 pages). Detection occurs before chunking (fail fast). Rejected with ERR-INGEST-003.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Oversized PDF rejected with ERR-INGEST-002 and size limit in message
  - [ ] Long query rejected with ERR-QUERY-003 and limit in message
  - [ ] Scanned PDF (< 100 chars/page average) rejected with ERR-INGEST-003
  - [ ] Chunk parameters documented with defaults in API documentation
  - [ ] Detection occurs before chunking to fail fast

### REQ-017: Phase 1 time budget per operation
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Target response times for Phase 1 operations (p95): Health check: <500ms, Query (with Ollama local): <10 seconds, Query (with OpenAI): <5 seconds, Ingest 10-page PDF: <30 seconds, Search (10k chunks): <500ms. Regression tolerance: p95 exceeding target by >20% triggers CI warning, >50% blocks merge.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Response times measured and logged
  - [ ] Slow responses include timing breakdown in debug logs
  - [ ] Docker Compose includes resource limits to ensure consistent performance
  - [ ] p95 exceeding target by >20% triggers CI warning
  - [ ] p95 exceeding target by >50% blocks merge

### REQ-018: Makefile targets for MVP workflow
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Required Makefile targets for Phase 1: make help (list all targets with descriptions), make up (start all services), make down (stop all services), make health (check all component health), make ingest FILE=path/to/file.pdf (ingest a PDF), make query Q="question text" (execute a query), make demo (run complete MVP workflow with sample PDF), make logs (tail logs from all services), make test (run integration tests).
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] make help output fits in terminal without scrolling
  - [ ] make demo completes in under 5 minutes on first run
  - [ ] All targets work on Linux and macOS
  - [ ] Targets fail fast with clear error messages

### REQ-019: API key authentication for all components
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: All Vektra components (core, index, ingest, admin) authenticate operator requests using API keys with Bearer token scheme. Keys are static credentials without expiration in Phase 1.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] All API endpoints except /health and /metrics require valid Bearer token
  - [ ] Invalid or missing token returns 401 with component name and remediation guidance
  - [ ] Valid token with insufficient scope returns 403
  - [ ] Token validation does not require external service calls

### REQ-020: API key management via admin component
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Admin component provides CRUD operations for API keys. Keys are stored with hashed values in PostgreSQL. Only admin can create, list, or revoke keys.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] POST /api-keys creates new key, returns plaintext value once
  - [ ] GET /api-keys lists keys with metadata (id, label, created_at, last_used_at) without values
  - [ ] DELETE /api-keys/{id} revokes key (soft delete with revoked_at)
  - [ ] Key values stored as bcrypt or argon2 hash

### REQ-021: Admin bootstrap authentication
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Admin component supports bootstrap authentication via VEKTRA_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_KEY environment variable. This allows initial API key creation before any keys exist in the system.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] VEKTRA_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_KEY env var accepted as Bearer token for POST /api-keys
  - [ ] Bootstrap key works regardless of database key count
  - [ ] Bootstrap key cannot list or revoke keys (create-only scope)
  - [ ] Startup logs warning if bootstrap key is set in production

### REQ-022: API key audit logging
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: All authenticated API requests are logged with key identifier for GDPR audit compliance. Logs include timestamp, key_id (not value), endpoint, and response status.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Each authenticated request logs key_id, endpoint, method, status_code, timestamp
  - [ ] Failed authentication attempts logged with reason (missing, invalid, revoked)
  - [ ] Logs written to structured format (JSON) for aggregation
  - [ ] key_id in logs allows tracing without exposing key value

### REQ-023: API key table schema with scope support
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: API key storage schema includes a scopes field from Phase 1, supporting multiple scopes per key (REQ-031). Schema: id (UUID primary key), key_hash (argon2id hash of key value), label (operator-assigned name, optional), scopes (array of: 'admin' | 'ingest' | 'query', default ['admin']), created_at (timestamp), last_used_at (timestamp, nullable), revoked_at (timestamp, nullable). Phase 1 behavior: all keys created via admin get ['admin'] scope by default, granting full access. The scopes field exists but enforcement is permissive in Phase 1. Scope values align with REQ-031 definitions.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Schema includes scopes column with NOT NULL constraint (array type)
  - [ ] Scope values are exactly: admin, ingest, query (CHECK constraint rejects unknown values)
  - [ ] Default scopes is ['admin'] for keys created via POST /api-keys
  - [ ] Scopes value returned in GET /api-keys response
  - [ ] Key hash uses argon2id algorithm
  - [ ] Tokens may have multiple scopes (REQ-031)

### REQ-024: Scope enforcement
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Scope enforcement uses REQ-031 scope terminology (admin, ingest, query). Phase 1 enforcement behavior: 'admin' scope grants access to all endpoints (superset of all permissions), 'ingest' and 'query' scopes stored but not enforced, unknown scope rejected with 403. Phase 2 (implemented): granular scope enforcement via require_scope() middleware — 'ingest' keys restricted to ingest endpoints, 'query' keys restricted to query endpoints.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Enforcement logic uses 'admin', 'ingest', 'query' scopes per REQ-031
  - [ ] All keys with 'admin' scope can access all endpoints
  - [ ] Keys with 'ingest' or 'query' scope: request succeeds in Phase 1 (enforcement deferred)
  - [ ] Unknown scope values rejected with 403 and ERR-AUTH-003
  - [ ] Scope enforcement documented as extensible in API documentation

### REQ-025: Health endpoint authentication: two-tier model
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Health endpoints implement two-tier authentication model. (1) Shallow health check (unauthenticated): Endpoint GET /health, returns {status: "healthy"|"degraded"|"unhealthy", timestamp: ISO8601}, no component enumeration/latency/version information, HTTP 200 for healthy/degraded, HTTP 503 for unhealthy, designed for load balancer probes and Kubernetes liveness checks. (2) Deep health check (authenticated): Endpoint GET /health?detail=full (requires Bearer token), returns component breakdown with name, status, latency_ms, includes version information and remediation hints for non-ok components, requires valid API key with any scope.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] GET /health without token returns {status, timestamp} only
  - [ ] GET /health without token returns HTTP 200 (healthy/degraded) or HTTP 503 (unhealthy)
  - [ ] GET /health?detail=full without token returns 401
  - [ ] GET /health?detail=full with valid token returns component array with name, status, latency_ms
  - [ ] Shallow response contains no component names, versions, or internal hostnames

### REQ-026: Acceptance criteria structure standard
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: All critical requirements must have acceptance criteria following three-part structure: scenario description (Given/When/Then), measurable success indicator, and failure handling specification.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Each REQ-00X includes at least one Given/When/Then scenario
  - [ ] Success indicators are machine-verifiable without human judgment
  - [ ] Failure scenarios specify expected error response

### REQ-027: REQ-005 checkpoint decomposition
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: The 30-minute exit criteria for MVP demonstration must be decomposed into discrete measurable checkpoints. Docker image pull time is excluded from the 30-minute clock.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] T+0:30 - docker compose up completes without error
  - [ ] T+2:00 - health endpoint returns 200
  - [ ] T+5:00 - sample document ingestion completes and is queryable
  - [ ] T+6:00 - query returns relevant response with source attribution
  - [ ] Total elapsed time from compose-up to query response under 10 minutes

### REQ-028: REQ-003 empty index response specification
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Query against empty index must return structured response guiding operator toward next action.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Given: No documents ingested
  - [ ] When: Query endpoint called with valid query
  - [ ] Then: Return HTTP 200 with message 'No documents indexed. Ingest documents using POST /ingest first.'
  - [ ] Response includes empty results array, not error status

### REQ-029: REQ-002 boundary behavior specification
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Document ingestion behavior at and around the 10MB threshold must be explicitly defined and testable.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Given: Document size < 10MB; When: POST /ingest; Then: Synchronous 200 response
  - [ ] Given: Document size = 10MB exactly; When: POST /ingest; Then: Synchronous 200 response (boundary inclusive)
  - [ ] Given: Document size > 10MB; When: POST /ingest; Then: 202 Accepted with job_id
  - [ ] Polling endpoint: GET /ingest/jobs/{id}/status returns pending|processing|indexed|failed (per BR-004)
  - [ ] Queryable within 60 seconds measured from 200/202 response

### REQ-030: Authentication error response contracts
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: API authentication chain must return structured error responses with specific codes for each failure mode.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Missing or malformed Authorization header: 401 with ERR-AUTH-001
  - [ ] Valid format but token not found or revoked: 401 with ERR-AUTH-001
  - [ ] Valid token but expired: 401 with ERR-AUTH-002 (Phase 2, reserved)
  - [ ] Valid token but insufficient scope: 403 with ERR-AUTH-003, body includes required_scope
  - [ ] All error responses use REQ-010 envelope with message and remediation
  - [ ] Error codes per REQ-041 (authoritative source)

### REQ-031: API scope definitions
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Three API scopes govern operation permissions. Scope names and permitted operations must be explicitly defined.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Scope 'admin': permits POST /api-keys, DELETE /api-keys/{id}, GET /api-keys, DELETE /documents/{id}, GET /admin
  - [ ] Scope 'ingest': permits POST /ingest, GET /ingest/jobs/{id}/status, POST /documents/{id}/chunks
  - [ ] Scope 'query': permits POST /query, POST /search, GET /providers
  - [ ] Any valid scope: permits GET /stats, GET /health?detail=full, GET /health/{component}, GET /health/memory
  - [ ] Bootstrap key has implicit 'admin' scope for key creation only
  - [ ] Tokens may have multiple scopes

### REQ-032: Integration acceptance test: full auth-ingest-query flow
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: End-to-end integration test validating the complete operator journey from bootstrap to query.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Given: Fresh deployment with BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY set
  - [ ] When: Use bootstrap key to create API key with scopes [ingest, query]
  - [ ] Then: Receive new API key in response
  - [ ] When: Use new key to POST /ingest with sample document
  - [ ] Then: Receive 200 or 202 with document/job ID
  - [ ] When: Poll until queryable (max 60s)
  - [ ] When: Use new key to POST /query with question about document
  - [ ] Then: Receive response with answer and source attribution
  - [ ] Complete flow executes in single automated test script

### REQ-033: Duplicate document handling
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Ingestion endpoint detects duplicate documents by content hash and returns idempotent success for identical content.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] POST /ingest with identical content hash returns 200 OK with existing document_id
  - [ ] Response body includes {id, status: 'exists', content_hash} for deduplicated uploads
  - [ ] POST /ingest with same filename but different content hash returns 409 Conflict
  - [ ] 409 response includes existing document_id and both content hashes

### REQ-034: Content hash algorithm specification
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Duplicate detection uses SHA-256 hash of raw file bytes for content identity.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] SHA-256 hash computed on raw uploaded file bytes (not extracted text)
  - [ ] Hash algorithm documented in API specification
  - [ ] Content hash returned in ingestion response for all documents

### REQ-035: Audit logging for deduplication events
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Deduplication events recorded as distinct action type in audit log.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Audit log records 'document_deduplicated' action when content hash matches
  - [ ] Log entry includes operator_id, timestamp, content_hash, existing document_id
  - [ ] Deduplication events queryable separately from new ingestion events

### REQ-036: Bootstrap key single-use enforcement
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Bootstrap key (VEKTRA_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_KEY) is consumed after first successful API key creation and becomes invalid for subsequent requests.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Given bootstrap key is set, when POST /api-keys succeeds, then subsequent requests with same key return 401
  - [ ] Successful bootstrap consumption logged to audit log with action 'bootstrap_key_consumed'
  - [ ] Error message on second attempt: 'Bootstrap key already used. Create additional keys using admin API key.'
  - [ ] Recovery from lost admin key requires container redeploy with new bootstrap key

### REQ-040: API endpoint path conventions
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: All REST endpoints follow consistent path patterns: Ingestion job status: GET /ingest/jobs/{id}/status (canonical path), Document resources: /documents/{id}, Query operations: /query prefix, Admin operations: /admin prefix. Consolidates REQ-014 and REQ-029 into single convention.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Single canonical path per resource type
  - [ ] No duplicate endpoints for same function
  - [ ] OpenAPI spec validates path conventions
  - [ ] GET /documents/{id}/status removed in favor of /ingest/jobs/{id}/status

### REQ-041: Unified authentication error codes
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Single authoritative list of authentication/authorization error codes: ERR-AUTH-001 (Invalid token - malformed, unrecognized, or revoked), ERR-AUTH-002 (Expired token - if token expiration is added in future), ERR-AUTH-003 (Insufficient scope - valid token but missing required scope), ERR-AUTH-004 (Rate limited - if rate limiting is added in future), ERR-AUTH-005 (Auth service unavailable). REQ-011 and REQ-030 reference this requirement as the authoritative source.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Error codes defined in shared schema
  - [ ] All components return these codes consistently
  - [ ] REQ-011 registry updated to reference these codes
  - [ ] REQ-030 error contracts aligned with these codes

### REQ-042: Streaming query responses
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: POST /query supports streaming responses via Server-Sent Events when client requests Accept: text/event-stream. Non-streaming behavior preserved for standard requests.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] First token delivered within 2s of request (assuming LLM provider responds)
  - [ ] Client disconnect terminates LLM request (no orphan processing)
  - [ ] Mid-stream LLM errors emit error event before stream close
  - [ ] Non-streaming requests (Accept: application/json) return complete response as before

### REQ-043: Configurable prompt templates
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Platform Operators can customize system and RAG prompt templates via configuration files without code changes. Templates use Jinja2 format with documented variables. Phase 1 scope limited to system prompts and RAG context injection prompts. Each loaded template is identified by a prompt_version (SHA-256 hash of content, first 8 chars) for traceability. See REQ-065 for prompt versioning details.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Template files loaded from configurable path with fallback to built-in defaults
  - [ ] Jinja2 template format supported
  - [ ] Template variables documented (available context per template type)
  - [ ] 2-3 built-in templates provided as examples
  - [ ] Integration test verifies custom template loading
  - [ ] Each template identified by prompt_version hash (REQ-065)

### REQ-044: Safeguard hook interface
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Extensible middleware skeleton for content safeguards. Phase 1 implements hook points with pass-through defaults; actual safeguard logic deferred to Phase 2.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] SafeguardHook protocol with pre_query, post_retrieval, pre_response methods
  - [ ] FastAPI Depends() integration pattern
  - [ ] Default pass-through implementation (no-op)
  - [ ] Less than 5ms latency overhead when no-op
  - [ ] Pre-query hook executes before SSE stream starts
  - [ ] Configurable hook chain via settings

### REQ-045: Word document text extraction
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: vektra-ingest extracts plain text from Word documents (.docx) using python-docx library. Phase 1 scope: paragraph and heading text only. Tables, images, embedded objects, and macros are ignored with warning logged.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Accepts .docx files (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
  - [ ] Extracts paragraph and heading text preserving reading order
  - [ ] Logs warning when skipping tables, images, or embedded objects
  - [ ] Returns empty result with error for corrupted or password-protected files

### REQ-046: PowerPoint presentation text extraction
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: vektra-ingest extracts plain text from PowerPoint files (.pptx) using python-pptx library. Phase 1 scope: slide titles, text boxes, and speaker notes. Charts, SmartArt, embedded media, and animations are ignored with warning logged.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Accepts .pptx files (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation)
  - [ ] Extracts slide titles, text boxes, and speaker notes in slide order
  - [ ] Logs warning when skipping charts, SmartArt, or embedded media
  - [ ] Returns empty result with error for corrupted or password-protected files

### REQ-047: Multi-provider LLM support (amends REQ-013)
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Platform supports multiple LLM providers with provider selection configurable at deployment time. No hardcoded default at platform level. Amends REQ-013 to include Anthropic and remove 'default' language per system constraint in CONTEXT.md.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama providers implemented
  - [ ] Provider selection via configuration (environment variable or config file)
  - [ ] Chat completion API abstraction works across all three providers
  - [ ] Provider swappable without code changes

### REQ-048: Namespace support for document isolation
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: vektra-index supports namespaces for logical document separation. All document operations (store, search, delete) are scoped to a namespace. Namespace is a first-class entity with its own database table including metadata (owner, quota, config overrides, GDPR retention). Phase 1: single default namespace ("default") pre-created via migration, metadata fields nullable and unenforced. Phase 2: multi-namespace with per-API-key namespace restrictions, quota enforcement, and per-namespace configuration overrides.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] `namespaces` table exists with id, display_name, owner_key_id, quota_chunks, quota_documents, config (JSONB), retention_days, created_at, updated_at
  - [ ] "default" namespace pre-created via Alembic migration
  - [ ] POST /documents/{id}/chunks accepts optional namespace parameter (default: "default")
  - [ ] POST /search accepts namespace parameter, searches only within specified namespace
  - [ ] DELETE /documents/{id} requires namespace parameter for explicit scoping
  - [ ] GET /stats accepts optional namespace filter
  - [ ] Cross-namespace queries not supported (by design)
  - [ ] Quota and config fields nullable in Phase 1 (enforcement deferred to Phase 2)

### REQ-049: Multi-turn conversation context
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Query endpoint supports multi-turn conversations by accepting an optional conversation_id. When provided, previous turns from the same conversation are included as context for the LLM. Phase 1: in-memory session storage (lost on container restart). Phase 2: persistent session storage.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] POST /query accepts optional conversation_id (UUID)
  - [ ] If conversation_id provided and exists, previous Q&A pairs included in LLM context
  - [ ] If conversation_id provided but not found, new conversation started with that ID
  - [ ] If conversation_id omitted, single-turn query (no history)
  - [ ] Maximum conversation history: 10 turns (configurable via VEKTRA_MAX_CONVERSATION_TURNS)
  - [ ] Conversation state stored in-memory (Phase 1), lost on restart
  - [ ] Response includes conversation_id for client to maintain continuity

### REQ-050: Pluggable vector store backend
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: vektra-index abstracts vector store operations behind a VectorStoreProvider Protocol, allowing deployment-time selection of backend. The search interface supports SearchMode (DENSE, SPARSE, HYBRID), QueryEmbedding (dense + optional sparse vector), and optional SearchFilters for metadata filtering. Phase 1: pgvector is the only implemented backend, SearchMode.DENSE only, sparse vector ignored, SearchFilters applied as WHERE clause. Phase 2: hybrid search (dense + sparse + RRF fusion), additional backends.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] VectorStoreProvider Protocol defined with store, search, delete, health_check
  - [ ] search() accepts QueryEmbedding (dense + optional sparse), SearchMode enum, optional SearchFilters
  - [ ] pgvector implementation of VectorStoreProvider
  - [ ] Phase 1: SearchMode.DENSE only, sparse vector ignored if provided
  - [ ] Backend selection via VEKTRA_VECTOR_STORE_PROVIDER env var (default: "pgvector")
  - [ ] Unknown provider value rejected at startup with clear error
  - [ ] Interface documented for future backend implementations

### REQ-051: Operator privacy: no conversation content access
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Platform Operators (admin scope) cannot access conversation content through any API. Audit logs record metadata (timestamps, IDs, endpoints) but never query text or response content. This ensures GDPR compliance and student privacy in educational deployments.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] No API endpoint exposes conversation content to admin scope
  - [ ] Audit logs contain only: timestamp, key_id, endpoint, method, status_code, request_id
  - [ ] Query text and response text never written to audit logs
  - [ ] Conversation content stored separately from audit data with different access controls
  - [ ] Admin dashboard shows only aggregate metrics, never individual conversations

### REQ-052: EmbeddingProvider Protocol
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Embedding generation abstracted behind EmbeddingProvider Protocol in vektra_shared. Separates embed_documents() from embed_query() to support asymmetric models (e.g., e5-large requires "query: ..." vs "passage: ..." prefixes). Single model instance shared between vektra-ingest and vektra-core to avoid double memory loading. Phase 1: SentenceTransformersProvider with all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Provider and model configurable via environment variables.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] EmbeddingProvider Protocol defined with embed_documents(), embed_query(), dimensions(), health_check()
  - [ ] Single model instance shared between vektra-ingest and vektra-core (no double loading)
  - [ ] Provider selection via VEKTRA_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER env var (default: "sentence-transformers")
  - [ ] Model selection via VEKTRA_EMBEDDING_MODEL env var (default: "all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
  - [ ] dimensions() returns vector dimensionality for schema validation

### REQ-053: QueryPipeline Protocol
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: RAG query pipeline abstracted behind QueryPipeline Protocol. execute() returns both QueryResponse and QueryTrace for observability. execute_stream() returns AsyncIterator for SSE streaming. Phase 1: SimpleQueryPipeline (embed -> search -> prompt -> LLM). Supports graceful degradation (REQ-059). Selectable via config.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] QueryPipeline Protocol defined with execute() and execute_stream()
  - [ ] execute() returns tuple of (QueryResponse, QueryTrace)
  - [ ] SimpleQueryPipeline implements current RAG flow behind the Protocol
  - [ ] Pipeline selection via VEKTRA_QUERY_PIPELINE env var (default: "simple")
  - [ ] Pipeline receives dependencies via constructor injection (EmbeddingProvider, VectorStoreProvider, LLMProvider, SafeguardHook)

### REQ-054: ChunkingStrategy Protocol
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Text chunking abstracted behind ChunkingStrategy Protocol. Receives AsyncIterator[DocumentChunk] from DocumentExtractor, returns AsyncIterator[DocumentChunk] with chunked output. Phase 1: FixedSizeChunking preserving REQ-016 parameters (1000 tokens, 200 overlap). Phase 2: DualStrategyChunking (text split with overlap, tables never split, parent-child hierarchy).
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] ChunkingStrategy Protocol defined with chunk() method
  - [ ] FixedSizeChunking implementation preserves REQ-016 behavior
  - [ ] Strategy selection via VEKTRA_CHUNKING_STRATEGY env var (default: "fixed")
  - [ ] Input and output are both AsyncIterator[DocumentChunk]

### REQ-055: Response and citation traceability
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**: Every query response includes a response_id (UUID) for downstream correlation, and every source citation includes a citation_id (UUID) for granular feedback. Phase 1: IDs generated and returned to client, no feedback endpoint. Phase 2: POST /feedback/{response_id} and POST /feedback/citation/{citation_id} enable quality improvement loops.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] QueryResponse includes response_id: UUID (v4)
  - [ ] Each SourceRef in response includes citation_id: UUID (v4)
  - [ ] response_id persisted in QueryTrace for correlation (REQ-060)
  - [ ] IDs included in JSON response to client
  - [ ] No feedback endpoint required in Phase 1

### REQ-056: Document versioning in data model
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: SourceDocument includes version (int, default 1) and supersedes_id (nullable FK to previous version). SearchResult includes document_version. Phase 1: version always 1, supersedes_id always null. Phase 2: re-ingestion of updated content creates new version instead of delete-then-reindex, preserving correlation between historical responses and document versions. **Phase 2 note**: when document versioning is active, re-ingestion of same filename with different content creates a new version (superseding REQ-033's 409 Conflict behavior for this case). The 409 behavior remains for Phase 1.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] SourceDocument schema includes version (NOT NULL, default 1)
  - [ ] SourceDocument schema includes supersedes_id (nullable FK to source_documents.id)
  - [ ] SearchResult includes document_version field
  - [ ] Existing Phase 1 behavior preserved (version=1 for all documents)
  - [ ] Phase 2: re-ingestion with same filename but different content creates version N+1 (not 409)

### REQ-057: Soft delete for documents
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Document deletion uses soft delete pattern for GDPR compliance. SourceDocument includes deleted_at (timestamp, nullable) and deletion_reason (enum: "user_request", "superseded", "expired"). All queries filter WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Phase 2: periodic cleanup job hard-deletes records past retention period. **Deduplication interaction**: content hash dedup checks (REQ-033, REQ-034) exclude soft-deleted documents (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Re-ingesting a soft-deleted document creates a new record.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] DELETE /documents/{id} sets deleted_at and deletion_reason instead of hard delete
  - [ ] All search and list queries exclude soft-deleted documents
  - [ ] Dedup checks (REQ-033) exclude soft-deleted documents
  - [ ] Audit log records deletion event with document_id and reason
  - [ ] Soft-deleted documents not returned by any API endpoint
  - [ ] Phase 2: arq cleanup job removes records past VEKTRA_RETENTION_DAYS

### REQ-058: Content type detection via magic bytes
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Ingest pipeline detects actual file content type via magic bytes (first bytes of file) before dispatching to DocumentExtractor. Dispatches based on detected type (more reliable than file extension). Logs warning on mismatch between detected and declared type. Uses python-magic library (~2MB, requires libmagic on Linux).
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Magic bytes detection runs before DocumentExtractor dispatch
  - [ ] Mismatch between detected and declared MIME type logged as warning
  - [ ] Dispatch uses detected type, not declared extension
  - [ ] Unsupported detected content type rejected with ERR-INGEST-001 and detected MIME in message

### REQ-059: LLM graceful degradation
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: LLM configuration supports optional fallback_model, fallback_timeout_ms (default 30000), and context_only_enabled (default true). When primary model times out, system switches to fallback model. When fallback also fails and context_only_enabled is true, system returns retrieved chunks without LLM synthesis. Client always receives value (relevant sources at minimum) instead of an error.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] LLMConfig includes fallback_model (string, nullable), fallback_timeout_ms (int), context_only_enabled (bool)
  - [ ] Primary model timeout triggers fallback attempt with structured log warning
  - [ ] Context-only response includes sources array, answer=null, context_only=true flag
  - [ ] Fallback and context-only events recorded in QueryTrace (REQ-060)

### REQ-060: QueryTrace for RAG observability
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Every query execution produces a QueryTrace with per-step timing, chunk references (IDs and scores), and pipeline metadata. QueryTrace is separate from audit logging and does not contain query text or response content (REQ-051 compliance preserved). Correlates with QueryResponse via response_id (REQ-055). Phase 1: emitted via structlog as JSON. Phase 2: dedicated storage with query API for RAG quality analysis.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] QueryTrace includes response_id, steps (list of StepTrace), total_duration_ms, chunks_retrieved (id + score), llm_model, prompt_version
  - [ ] Each StepTrace includes name, duration_ms, metadata dict
  - [ ] QueryTrace does NOT contain query text or response text
  - [ ] Emitted as structured log event separate from audit log
  - [ ] response_id links QueryTrace to QueryResponse

### REQ-061: EventEmitter interface
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Internal event hook system with EventEmitter Protocol. Phase 1: NoOpEventEmitter (all events silently discarded). Emission points defined at: document.indexed, document.failed, query.completed, safeguard.triggered, apikey.created, apikey.revoked. Phase 2: WebhookEventEmitter with HMAC-SHA256 signature verification.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] EventEmitter Protocol defined with async emit(event_type: str, payload: dict)
  - [ ] NoOpEventEmitter as default implementation
  - [ ] emit() calls present at all documented emission points in production code
  - [ ] Less than 1ms overhead with NoOp implementation
  - [ ] Event type names follow dotted convention (e.g., "document.indexed")

### REQ-062: ProviderRegistry pattern
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Unified registry for all Protocol implementations selectable via configuration. Consistent env var pattern: VEKTRA_{CATEGORY}_PROVIDER or VEKTRA_{CATEGORY} for all pluggable components. Phase 1: dict-based registry populated at startup. Phase 2: extensible with Python entry_points for plugin discovery.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] ProviderRegistry in vektra_shared with register(), get(), list() methods
  - [ ] All Protocol implementations registered during application startup
  - [ ] Consistent VEKTRA_* env var pattern for provider selection
  - [ ] Unknown provider name rejected at startup with clear error listing available options
  - [ ] list() returns available providers per category for diagnostics

### REQ-063: Chunk metadata filtering
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: VectorStoreProvider.search() accepts optional filters parameter for metadata-based filtering. ChunkMetadata defines generic filterable fields: content_type, language, plus arbitrary key-value pairs stored in JSONB. Phase 1: filters applied as WHERE clause on JSONB metadata column with GIN index. Metadata fields populated optionally during ingest via key-value pairs. Domain-specific fields (e.g., course_id, module_id, academic_year for vektra-learn) are defined by the vertical in Phase 2 and stored in the same JSONB column without requiring schema changes.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] search() accepts filters: SearchFilters | None parameter
  - [ ] ChunkMetadata type defines generic filterable fields (content_type, language) plus arbitrary keys
  - [ ] GIN index created on document_chunks.metadata JSONB column
  - [ ] Filtering combined with vector similarity in single SQL query (not post-filtering)
  - [ ] None filters preserves current behavior (no additional filtering)
  - [ ] Arbitrary metadata keys accepted during ingest without schema changes

### REQ-064: Zero-downtime reindex via index_version
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Document chunks include index_version (int, default 1). All search queries filter by active index version (VEKTRA_ACTIVE_INDEX_VERSION env var, default 1). Enables embedding model or chunking strategy changes without downtime: new chunks created with incremented version alongside old, atomic switch via config change, cleanup of old version afterwards. Phase 1: all chunks at version 1, filter applied in queries. Phase 2: reindex API with progress tracking.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] document_chunks table includes index_version (NOT NULL, default 1)
  - [ ] B-tree index on index_version column
  - [ ] All search queries include WHERE index_version = active_version filter
  - [ ] VEKTRA_ACTIVE_INDEX_VERSION env var controls active version (default: 1)
  - [ ] Embedding model change documented as requiring full reindex via index_version pattern

### REQ-065: Prompt versioning
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: Every prompt template (REQ-043) is identified by a prompt_version computed as truncated SHA-256 hash of template content (first 8 hex chars). prompt_version recorded in QueryTrace (REQ-060) for correlation between template changes and response quality. Amends REQ-043.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] prompt_version computed as SHA-256(template_content)[:8] on template load
  - [ ] prompt_version included in QueryTrace
  - [ ] Template content change produces different prompt_version
  - [ ] Built-in default templates have documented prompt_version values

### REQ-066: No relevant context response
- **Priority**: should
- **Description**: When all retrieved chunks score below the minimum relevance threshold (VEKTRA_MIN_RELEVANCE_SCORE), the system returns a graceful response with `no_relevant_context=true` instead of synthesizing an answer from irrelevant context. The response answer field explains that no relevant information was found and suggests ingesting additional documents. Sources array is empty. This is a distinct path from LLM degradation (REQ-059): retrieval succeeded but produced no usable results. Implemented in SimpleQueryPipeline (ARCH-056).
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Given all retrieved chunks score below VEKTRA_MIN_RELEVANCE_SCORE, Then QueryResponse.no_relevant_context=True
  - [ ] Given no_relevant_context=True, Then sources array is empty
  - [ ] Given no_relevant_context=True, Then answer field contains a message explaining no relevant content was found (not null, not an error)
  - [ ] Given no_relevant_context=True, Then retrieval_filter StepTrace records chunks_before, chunks_after=0, threshold value
  - [ ] Given no_relevant_context=True, Then HTTP status is 200 (not an error response)

### Assessment discussion chatbot (v1)

*Merged from session `20261101-091559-specs-assessment-discussion-chatbot` (2026-11-01). IDs renumbered for merge; references to REQ ≤ 066, NFR ≤ 013, BR ≤ 005 are pre-existing platform requirements. Conflicts CONF-001..008 are session-local records (see session file).*

#### REQ-067: Server-authoritative discussion lifecycle per (student, activity)
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Lifecycle: NOT_ELIGIBLE -> ELIGIBLE -> STARTING (transient) -> ACTIVE (<-> OUTAGE) ->
  CLOSED(reason). Close reasons: finished | timed_out | service_failure | budget_exhausted |
  terminated_by_teacher | access_revoked.
  A session is CONSUMED if and only if the opening bot message has been generated AND persisted
  server-side. STARTING commits to ACTIVE or rolls back to ELIGIBLE (REQ-071). Delivery status is
  tracked separately (REQ-075). A teacher reset (REQ-087) creates session #N+1. At most one
  non-CLOSED session per (student, activity) exists at any time.
  Gate sets:
  - START gates = all of BR-006 (a)-(h), evaluated at render and at Start.
  - IN-SESSION gates = token valid, owner match, not impersonated, session in ACTIVE or OUTAGE,
    deadline not passed. Evaluated on every request while the session is open. A failed
    in-session gate rejects the request (audit-logged) WITHOUT changing session state.
  The only state-changing exception: if the student loses enrolment or the student role while
  ACTIVE or OUTAGE, the session closes as CLOSED(access_revoked) and the transcript is generated
  and delivered.
  Disable (REQ-081), another student's override (BR-006) and withdrawn release (BR-008) do not
  affect sessions that are already ACTIVE.
  Fail closed. Nothing held by the browser or rendered by Moodle is authoritative. State names and
  storage are for design.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Concurrent starts (double-click, two tabs) produce exactly one STARTING/ACTIVE session
  - [ ] Fine twice -> one close + one transcript
  - [ ] After CLOSED, any message, token re-mint or new session is rejected unless a reset has created #N+1
  - [ ] Negating any single START gate hides or disables the button AND makes the Start API call fail
  - [ ] consumed == exists(persisted opening bot turn) for every record
  - [ ] Disable while ACTIVE -> messages are still accepted
  - [ ] Extending another student's override while ACTIVE -> session unaffected
  - [ ] Unenrol while ACTIVE -> CLOSED(access_revoked) and the transcript is generated
  - [ ] A failed in-session gate -> request rejected, state unchanged, audit event
- **Related**: REQ-071, REQ-075, REQ-081, BR-006, BR-008

#### REQ-068: Student entry point, button states and pre-session screen
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Entry is on the results page (quiz attempt review; assignment feedback). Button states:
  (1) not enabled: no button;
  (2) not fully graded (BR-014) OR not released: disabled, "Disponibile quando la valutazione
      sarà pubblicata";
  (3) graded, gate not open (incl. in-progress or overdue attempts, the C7 NOT_AVAILABLE state):
      disabled. The date is shown only if it equals the activity's own effective close or the
      student's own override, else "Disponibile dopo la chiusura definitiva dell'attività". No
      other student's data reaches the student;
  (4) eligible: enabled;
  (5) ACTIVE: "Riprendi" + minutes left;
  (6) CLOSED with no reset pending: status line + date + transcript links #1..#N;
  (7) temporarily unavailable: disabled, non-technical message;
  (8) "login as": disabled;
  (9) non-selected attempt: pointer to attempt #k;
  (10) reset granted, not yet started: "Discuti questa prova (sessione #N)" + links #1..#N-1;
  (11) NEW, end date passed with no session open: "Discussione non più disponibile dal <data>",
       with transcript links if any.
  Pre-session screen:
  - duration, with "se non corrisponde, contatta il docente prima di iniziare";
  - one session; no grade change; transcript to the teacher and an identical copy to the student;
  - recipients by role and name;
  - "Materiale del corso: usato / non usato"; AI disclosure; limits; privacy summary + link;
  - the enrolment-dependency statement (REQ-093); the previous-sessions line for N > 1;
  - D2 (SHOULD): each file's status predicted from metadata, plus "Se un file importante non può
    essere letto, potrai discuterne all'orale".
  Dismissing consumes nothing. Pre-flight shows "Preparazione della discussione…", announced
  once.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Every state is reproducible on 4.3 and 5.2 x quiz and assignment, incl. abandoned-attempt and end-date fixtures
  - [ ] Gate held by another student's extension -> no date, name or count in student HTML or API
  - [ ] After a reset -> state (10); after the end date -> state (11) and a crafted Start is rejected
  - [ ] BR-014 fixtures (an ungraded essay, a regrade in progress, a rubric criterion without a level) -> state (2) and API Start refused; a quiz with description and zero-mark items still becomes ELIGIBLE
  - [ ] Disabled buttons are focusable with an exposed reason; no technical errors shown
  - [ ] Dismissing the pre-session screen leaves the record ELIGIBLE
- **Related**: BR-006, BR-010, BR-012, BR-014, REQ-084, REQ-087, REQ-093, REQ-101

#### REQ-069: Server wall-clock time limit with resume
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Deadline = commit time (opening message persisted) + cap + extra time + credited outage
  (REQ-086). Only the server fixes and extends it; cold-start latency up to T is not charged.
  Browser close, reload and the student's own network drop neither end nor pause the session, and
  earn no credit. The owner resumes the SAME session, with full history, only from the results
  page in a fresh authenticated Moodle session. Client time is ignored. Two tabs are serialized
  ("attendi la risposta"). A message sent during a drop is shown as delivered or as not sent with
  resend, and is never lost.
  Warnings at 5 and 1 min always, plus at 10 min when the duration is 30 min or more. They are
  computed against the CURRENT deadline, including any outage credit, and each is announced once
  via a polite live region. The timer updates per minute.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Reload resumes the same session id with full history; remaining time within 1 s of the server
  - [ ] Tampering with the client timer has no effect
  - [ ] A second tab sending while a reply is pending is refused; no duplicate turn
  - [ ] The student's own 3-min network drop extends the deadline by 0
  - [ ] With an outage credit of X min, every warning fires at the new deadline minus 10/5/1 min (+/-5 s), and none fires against the old deadline
  - [ ] Boundary tests +/-1 s (UTC) pass
- **Related**: REQ-078, REQ-086

#### REQ-070: Timeout handling and server-side close of abandoned sessions
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  At the deadline, student input is locked. A reply already being generated may finish within a
  grace window (default 60 s, configurable); otherwise the transcript marks it
  "risposta interrotta". Text typed but not sent is excluded. A server-side process closes
  sessions past their deadline as CLOSED(timed_out) and triggers the transcript without a client.
  It NEVER closes a session while that session is in OUTAGE; the outage REQ governs that case.
  The sweeper mechanism is for design.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] No student message is accepted after the deadline
  - [ ] No assistant message is stored after deadline + grace
  - [ ] Both branches (reply finishes within grace / reply is cut off) are verified with a slowed provider
  - [ ] With the browser closed, the session reaches CLOSED(timed_out) and a transcript exists within 5 min of the deadline
  - [ ] A session in OUTAGE at its nominal deadline is not closed as timed_out
- **Related**: REQ-069

#### REQ-071: Start pre-flight, commit and rollback; failures at start never consume the session
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  On Start, the backend runs a pre-flight check:
  - eligibility re-check (BR-006, including BR-010);
  - not an impersonated ("login as") session;
  - admission capacity;
  - LLM provider reachable;
  - Moodle grading context read and snapshot (BR-008), with context assembly per BR-011.
  If any check fails, nothing is created and the record stays ELIGIBLE. If all pass, the record
  enters STARTING. It commits to ACTIVE when the opening bot message is generated AND persisted
  server-side within T (default 60 s). Otherwise it rolls back to ELIGIBLE, nothing is consumed,
  and the rollback is audit-logged with a reason.
  Rollback is triggered ONLY by server-attributable failures. A client disconnect, reload or tab
  close during STARTING never triggers it: the session commits normally and the stored message is
  visible on resume. No bot output or attempt content is returned to the client before commit.
  Abuse cap (defaults, operator-configurable, values for the pilot):
  - at most 5 Start attempts per (student, activity) per hour; beyond that, "Riprova tra X minuti";
  - after 3 consecutive system rollbacks the student sees "Problema tecnico persistente: non hai
    perso la tua sessione. Il docente è stato avvisato", and the teacher and the operator are
    notified.
  Student messages: "Non è stato possibile avviare la discussione; non hai perso la tua sessione.
  Riprova più tardi." / "Servizio momentaneamente non disponibile" / "Troppi utenti, riprova più
  tardi".

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] With the provider stopped, a start attempt leaves the record ELIGIBLE and the button still enabled
  - [ ] With the concurrency limit at K, the (K+1)th start is refused and remains ELIGIBLE
  - [ ] With the Moodle web service unreachable, the start is refused, nothing is consumed, and the operator is alerted
  - [ ] A provider that does not persist the opening message within T leads to rollback to ELIGIBLE plus an audit event
  - [ ] A client that disconnects after Start while the server persists the opening message leads to a consumed session, with the message visible on resume
  - [ ] No attempt content or bot text appears in any response before commit
  - [ ] The 6th Start within one hour is refused; 3 consecutive rollbacks notify the teacher and the operator
- **Related**: REQ-067, BR-006, BR-011, REQ-059

#### REQ-072: Finish action and closing screen
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  A Finish ("Fine") button with a confirmation step closes the session as CLOSED(finished). Input
  is then disabled. The closing screen states "Sessione conclusa il <data>; trascrizione inviata
  al docente" and offers "Visualizza / scarica la tua trascrizione" (student transcript REQ).

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Confirming Fine moves the record to CLOSED(finished) and creates exactly one transcript
  - [ ] Cancelling the confirmation keeps the session ACTIVE, and the deadline is unchanged
  - [ ] The transcript link on the closing screen works as soon as the transcript is generated, independent of email status
- **Related**: REQ-067

#### REQ-073: Contest handling verification
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Verifiable behaviour for the no-grade-change rule when students contest or attempt adversarial
  manipulation, including prompt injection embedded in the student's own submission.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] The fixed grade statement appears verbatim in 100% of transcripts
  - [ ] An adversarial suite of at least 30 prompts (including injection inside the submission) yields 0 assistant claims that the grade was or will be changed
  - [ ] Moodle grade, rubric and feedback for the attempt are byte-identical before and after a session
  - [ ] The service-account external service's function list contains no grade-write function (REQ-079 as amended)
- **Related**: REQ-044

#### REQ-074: Transcript content and integrity
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Exactly one transcript per closed session; student and teacher copies IDENTICAL. Content is
  ONLY a system-rendered header + turns: no system prompt, context, rubric definition beyond what
  the student can see, solution, override holder or reset reason.
  HEADER (never LLM-generated):
  - course, activity, student;
  - "Sessione #N di M" with earlier sessions (number, date, close reason);
    "contesto sessioni precedenti: sì/no";
  - "tentativo #k di M" + method;
  - grade at start; the grade at close only if released, else the neutral notice;
  - cap + extra (never the reason); timestamps; close reason (6-value vocabulary);
  - outage intervals + credited total; failed start attempts;
  - fixed BR-009 statement;
  - config snapshot (flags and values only);
  - D1: per-file status list (REQ-101) and conversation language(s) (REQ-100).
  BODY: timestamped, role-labelled, escaped turns.
  - Turns replaced by the safeguard are marked "[risposta sostituita dal sistema]".
  - Turns with a post-check value replacement are marked (REQ-096).
  - Student error flags (REQ-103, if built) are marked.
  - D1: "PUNTI CONTESTATI" is MUST (product-owner decision R8), in the REQ-097 format, labelled
    "Riepilogo generato dall'assistente".
  Format and serving per BR-016.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Transcript count == CLOSED count; copies hash-equal
  - [ ] 0 canaries for system prompt, solution text, pasted rubric or reset reason; regrade not released -> 0 occurrences of the new grade
  - [ ] Injected header-like text renders inert; every safeguard or post-check replacement is marked in both copies
  - [ ] The header lists every file with exactly one status and the conversation language(s)
  - [ ] Every contest exchange that reaches the restate step yields a 'Punti contestati' entry (REQ-097)
- **Related**: BR-009, BR-010, BR-011, BR-016, REQ-096, REQ-097, REQ-100, REQ-101, REQ-103

#### REQ-075: Durable transcript delivery by Vektra SMTP
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  The transcript is persisted (encrypted at rest) BEFORE any send attempt. It is sent through
  Vektra's own SMTP over mandatory TLS, with no plaintext fallback. Failed sends are retried with
  backoff over a configurable window: proposals range from 24 h to 72 h, and the value is to be
  set. Delivery status is PENDING -> SENT, or RETRYING -> FAILED. A transcript is marked SENT
  only when the SMTP relay has accepted it. One email is sent per closed session, with course,
  activity and student in the subject. FAILED transcripts are visible to the teacher and to the
  operator (metadata only).

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] With SMTP down for 2 h and then restored, every pending transcript is delivered exactly once (verified on a test mail sink)
  - [ ] No transcript is marked SENT without relay acceptance
  - [ ] At least 99% of closed sessions are SENT or downloadable within 15 min of close
- **Related**: REQ-051

#### REQ-076: Teacher in-Moodle session list and transcript download
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Graders of THAT activity see, per student, sessions #1..#N with:
  - state and close reason (including access_revoked);
  - delivery status, including bounces;
  - reset count and reset reasons (teacher-only);
  - authenticated download and resend;
  - the reset action (REQ-087) and the extra-time setting (REQ-078).
  The gate panel shows the effective opening date and which override holds it, by name only and
  never the reason, and only to users who already have the Moodle capability to see overrides. If
  the activity is NOT_AVAILABLE because of the C7 fallback, it shows that reason. Should: a hint
  when the override holding the gate belongs to a suspended or unenrolled user. No cross-course
  access.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] A non-grader or other-course teacher gets an authorization error
  - [ ] A FAILED transcript can be downloaded
  - [ ] The reset reason is visible in the list and absent from transcripts
  - [ ] C7 fallback NOT_AVAILABLE -> the reason is shown in the list
- **Related**: REQ-075, REQ-078, REQ-087, REQ-091

#### REQ-077: Teacher configuration in the activity settings page
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  A section visible to activity editors only. Fields:
  - enable;
  - cap 5-120 min;
  - rubric source (Moodle rubric for assignments / pasted text for quizzes). Help text (BR-011
    block): "Il testo della griglia può essere mostrato allo studente così com'è: non inserire
    risposte attese o soluzioni (usa il campo Soluzione)";
  - optional solution text;
  - "mostra soluzione nella discussione" (default OFF). Help text: when OFF, the solution and
    review-hidden content never reach the model; quiz detail is reduced where HTML cannot be
    filtered. D3: "Con questa opzione disattivata l'assistente non riceve la soluzione e non deve
    fornirla, ma per domande risolvibili autonomamente non è possibile garantirlo al 100%: evita
    di abilitare la discussione su domande che riutilizzerai. Ricorda inoltre che lo studente
    riceve una copia della trascrizione." A warning appears when ON;
  - recipients (REQ-082); RAG (default OFF);
  - the C7 opening date (REQ-091, fallback only);
  - NEW (product-owner decision): optional "Discussione disponibile fino al" (date-time). Empty
    means no limit, until retention. It must be later than the effective opening (BR-006(d) or
    REQ-091). After it: no new Starts (BR-006(i), REQ-068 state 11); sessions in ACTIVE or
    OUTAGE run to their normal end; resets are refused unless the date is moved (REQ-087). If the
    effective opening later moves past it, a warning appears. Changes are audited.
  The section shows the computed opening condition and the end date, and warns if review options
  hide content.
  Enable is refused for:
  - a quiz without a close date, or an assignment without a cut-off (BR-007);
  - Moodle-rubric source without a rubric; an empty pasted rubric;
  - team submission;
  - MARKING-GUIDE grading (EX-023);
  - privacy settings unset; admin check red (read-only).
  Validation per BR-013. Changes apply only to sessions not yet started and are audited
  old/new.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] New activity: RAG OFF and mostra soluzione OFF; end date empty
  - [ ] Enable on: no quiz close date / no assignment cut-off / team submission / marking guide / empty pasted rubric -> field-level error
  - [ ] BR-013 boundaries: 20,000 characters accepted, 20,001 refused; cap 4 and 121 refused; total duration 241 min refused, 240 accepted; extra time > +100% requires confirmation; each error names the range
  - [ ] End date not after the effective opening -> field error; after the end date, Start refused while an ACTIVE session continues to its normal end
  - [ ] Help texts contain the pasted-rubric line and the D3 sentence
  - [ ] A quiz in 'separate groups' mode can be enabled; changing the cap after start does not alter that session's deadline; every change audited old/new
- **Related**: BR-006, BR-007, BR-011, BR-013, REQ-081, REQ-082, REQ-087, REQ-091, REQ-099, EX-023

#### REQ-078: Per-student extra time (accommodations)
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Before a student starts, the teacher can grant that student extra session time, in minutes or as
  a percentage, from the discussion settings or the teacher list (REQ-076). This MUST ship in v1
  as a manual setting regardless of the outcome of OQ-025. It is required by WCAG 2.2.1 Timing
  Adjustable and Italian law (L.17/1999, L.170/2010). The student sees the extended duration on
  the pre-session screen. The transcript records only the granted duration, never the reason.
  Should: prefill from the student's Moodle time-limit overrides, if OQ-025 confirms feasibility.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] +50% on a 30-min cap produces a 45-min server deadline (plus any outage credit)
  - [ ] Extra time cannot be changed for a session that is ACTIVE or CLOSED
  - [ ] Neither the transcript nor any student-visible text discloses the reason
- **Related**: REQ-069, OQ-025

#### REQ-079: Site admin setup check for the dedicated service account
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Provisioning the dedicated Moodle service account is an install prerequisite. A "Verifica
  configurazione" check reports each item by name as OK or MISSING:
  - the token works;
  - the required reads succeed (grades, rubric instances and definitions, submissions, quiz
    reviews regardless of review options);
  - interactive login is disabled, via the `webservice` authentication method (auth_webservice
    enabled on the site). `auth=nologin` is NOT usable: Moodle refuses web-service access to
    nologin accounts (`wsaccessusernologin`, verified on 4.3 and 5.2 by the OQ-025 spike);
  - the account is NOT a site admin;
  - the account is NOT the ingestion account;
  - a probe of a denied function fails;
  - the external service's function list contains NO grade-write function (no function that
    writes grades, feedback, rubric fillings or submission status). Read-only capabilities that
    Moodle bundles with grading (e.g. moodle/grade:managegradingforms, needed to read rubric
    definitions) are permitted, because the WS layer can only call functions on the list.
    *(Amended 2026-11-01, coordinator decision: the literal "no grade-write capability" cannot
    hold, since reading rubrics requires managegradingforms.)*
  Spike-verified minimal role (OQ-025, 2026-11-01; read-only, no grade-write capability needed):
  webservice/rest:use, moodle/course:view, mod/quiz:viewreports, mod/quiz:viewoverrides (5.x),
  mod/assign:viewgrades, moodle/grade:viewall, moodle/grade:managegradingforms (rubric fillings
  only), moodle/role:review (grader listing), plus the view-level capabilities listed in the spike
  report. mod/assign:grade is NOT required. The external service must allow file download
  (`downloadfiles`).
  The feature stays unavailable until every item passes. Capabilities are never granted
  automatically. Token rotation does not affect ACTIVE sessions. A revoked token fails closed:
  eligible students see "temporarily unavailable" and nothing is consumed, and the operator is
  alerted.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] A check against the ingestion account, a site-admin account, or an external service whose function list includes a grade-write function fails and names the failing item
  - [ ] After token revocation, start attempts are refused without consumption and an operator alert is raised

#### REQ-080: Operator configuration and metadata-only monitoring
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  The operator configures SMTP (TLS) with a test send, the provider, the concurrency limit, the
  sweeper interval, the retry policy, retention and per-session limits. Monitoring offers
  content-free counters and alerts: sessions by state, close reasons, delivery failures,
  transcripts stuck in RETRYING. Resend works by session id without exposing content, and goes
  ONLY to that session's re-resolved recipients (REQ-082); the operator can never set or change
  a recipient. Application and mail logs contain no bodies. Purges are audited.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] An operator credential reading content gets 403
  - [ ] A canary grep of logs and mail logs returns 0
  - [ ] A resend API call carrying a recipient parameter is rejected
  - [ ] After purge, the row count of purged content is 0 and only audit metadata remains
- **Related**: REQ-082, REQ-051, NFR-007, NFR-008

#### REQ-081: Teacher disables discussion, or terminates active sessions
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Disabling blocks new starts and new token mints immediately. By default, ACTIVE sessions run to
  their normal end and deliver.
  The settings form shows "N sessioni attive". An explicit "termina subito" action, with
  confirmation stating N and a mandatory reason, closes those sessions as
  CLOSED(terminated_by_teacher). Their transcripts are generated and delivered, and the student
  sees "Sessione chiusa dal docente; trascrizione disponibile". A terminated session counts as
  consumed; a teacher reset is available.
  Re-enabling never reopens CLOSED sessions. Should: a site-admin per-activity emergency stop with
  the same effect.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] After disable, a start or token mint on an ELIGIBLE record is refused
  - [ ] After disable without 'termina subito', ACTIVE sessions reach finished or timed_out normally
  - [ ] 'Termina subito' moves all N sessions to CLOSED(terminated_by_teacher), produces N transcripts and an audit entry with the reason
  - [ ] After re-enable, a CLOSED record stays CLOSED
- **Related**: REQ-085

#### REQ-082: Transcript recipients: course graders, optional allowlisted free text
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  MUST:
  - Recipients default to the configuring teacher's Moodle address. Up to 3 recipients.
  - Each recipient is a user with grading capability in the course, with the address resolved
    from Moodle.
  - Recipients are re-resolved at send time. A recipient who has lost the capability is replaced
    by the course's current graders, and this is audited.
  - The pre-session screen names the recipients by role and name.
  - Each recipient gets one email per session (exactly-once is counted per recipient, REQ-075).
  - Bounces appear in REQ-076. Every recipient change is audited.
  SHOULD: free-text recipient overrides. They are offered ONLY together with a domain allowlist
  maintained by the site admin AND the change audit, which are MUST whenever free-text recipients
  exist. With an empty allowlist, no free text is allowed. If free-text overrides slip from v1,
  recipients are Moodle-resolved graders only. Validation errors list the allowed domains.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Free text outside the allowlist, or with an empty allowlist -> field-level error
  - [ ] A 4th recipient is refused
  - [ ] A recipient who lost the capability -> course graders, audited
  - [ ] Each change audited old/new
  - [ ] Build without free-text overrides -> the form offers only Moodle-resolved graders
- **Related**: REQ-075, REQ-077, REQ-080

#### REQ-083: Per-session abuse and cost limits
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Each session has limits on message length, message rate and total tokens. They are
  operator-configurable, with generous defaults: fewer than 1% of pilot sessions should hit them,
  and a realistic 120-min session never exhausts the budget. The defaults are sized before the
  pilot on a reference 120-min session.
  - Character counter via aria-describedby, not announced per keystroke.
  - Over-length messages are rejected client- AND server-side before any LLM call.
  - Rate limit: "Attendi qualche secondo".
  - Warning at 80% of the token budget. At exhaustion -> CLOSED(budget_exhausted) + transcript.
  - Limits are shown on the pre-session screen.
  - Retries during an outage, and earlier-session turns included under REQ-087, do not count
    against the budget.
  - Hitting a limit never earns outage credit.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Over-length message rejected, 0 LLM calls
  - [ ] Budget exhausted -> CLOSED(budget_exhausted) + exactly one transcript
  - [ ] Rate-limited or over-length -> deadline +0
- **Related**: REQ-080, REQ-087

#### REQ-084: Moodle 'login as' sessions cannot start or access a discussion
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  When an admin or teacher is using Moodle's "login as" on a student, the button is disabled with
  "Non disponibile in modalità accesso come altro utente". No token is minted, and the backend
  rejects any such token. There is no Start, resume, message, consumption, rollback or view of
  the student's transcript. The rejection is audited as loginas_rejected. The detection mechanism
  is for design.

- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] A start, resume or transcript request from a 'login as' session is refused, the record stays as it was, and 0 session rows are created
  - [ ] A loginas_rejected audit event is recorded
- **Related**: NFR-014, REQ-085

#### REQ-085: Minimum audit event set for discussions
- **Priority**: must
- **Description**:

  Content-free events (IDs, timestamps, reason codes):
  - token mint; Start; start_rollback (+reason); rollback/start-rate cap hit; commit;
  - outage_start / outage_end (+credited seconds);
  - close (+reason, including access_revoked); in-session gate rejection;
  - grade_claim_replaced;
  - transcript generated; each delivery attempt and result (per recipient);
  - student view or download; teacher download;
  - reset (+#N, reason stored in audit but hidden from operators); reset_notice_sent (if
    REQ-092 is adopted);
